_comment: WHY EACH COMMAND LOOKS LIKE THIS.
1. THE INTERPRETER IS RESOLVED, AND LASERBRAIN_PYTHON WINS. Naming `python3` is wrong on
Windows and anywhere the interpreter is `python`. Resolving it is still not enough:
the case that actually happens is a `python3` that EXISTS and cannot import laserbrain,
because the user installed into a venv or with pipx. LASERBRAIN_PYTHON lets them say
which interpreter has it. Every mcp-server.mjs already reads that variable (line 689);
the hooks were the one component that ignored it.
2. IT SAYS SO WHEN IT CANNOT RUN. The previous form ended in `|| exit 0`, so a missing
package produced no output at all: the plugin installed, the MCP tools worked because
they are a hosted HTTP server needing no Python, and the hooks never ran. Nothing
distinguished that from a quiet session. It now names the interpreter it tried, once,
guarded by a marker keyed on that interpreter's path so a changed interpreter warns
again and an unchanged one does not repeat on every tool call.
3. IT STILL FAILS OPEN. Every branch reaches `exit 0`. A hook that denied because it could
not load itself would brick every tool call in the session.
4. DENIAL DOES NOT TRAVEL BY EXIT CODE. It is stdout JSON —
hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision, lb_gate.py:712 — so exiting 0 cannot suppress a
real block.
5. lb_safety IS HERE. It was missing until 2026-08-29, so every installer got the
goal-drift gate and no destructive-command guard.

hooks.command: LB_PY=$(command -v "${LASERBRAIN_PYTHON:-}" 2>/dev/null || command -v python3 || command -v python); if [ -n "$LB_PY" ] && "$LB_PY" -c 'import laserbrain' 2>/dev/null; then LASERBRAIN_AGENT=claude "$LB_PY" -m laserbrain.hooks.lb_gate; else M="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/laserbrain-inert-$(printf %s "${LB_PY:-none}" | tr -c 'a-zA-Z0-9' _)"; [ -f "$M" ] || { : >"$M"; printf 'laserbrain hooks are inert: %s cannot import laserbrain. Run: pip install laserbrain into that interpreter, or set LASERBRAIN_PYTHON.\n' "${LB_PY:-no python found}" >&2; }; fi; exit 0
